data.turoyo: Azze u maṣri l gabe, omər: "Mir Kanun." Omər: "Ha." Omər: "Hali u abro d qwilox aʕmi."
data.translation: Darauf kam der Aegypter zu ihm und sagte: "Mir Kanun, gib mir den Sohn, den du mir vertragsmässig versprochen hast".

rationale: Thin I Preterit/1; second-person promise with ʕam partner and promised-son antecedent.

summary: All three occurrences fit inherited promising senses. I pairs a promiser with ʕam partner and d-content; II additionally expresses the promised daughter as direct patient.
The Arabic etymological 'speak/say' gloss is not itself evidence of a general speech sense in these tokens.
PrS 58/16 and inherited prs 157/9 have essentially the same promise clause; this is a citation discrepancy to verify, not independent thin-cell evidence.
Jan 2.12/2827 is a continuous Arabic quotation, including al bayt, min al awwali and yaqul rab aǧ ǧənud. yaqul is not evidence for the Turoyo I qwile/qowəl or II mqawele/mqawəl paradigms.

Round 1 already distinguishes productive Turoyo promising from the Arabic etymological speak/say range. This quotation supplies no contrary vernacular evidence, so the inherited glosses and round-1 proposals remain unchanged. Supplied English is machine translation; no quotation is added.
Verify whether prs 157/9 and supplied PrS 58/16 reflect edition numbering or a miscitation before changing the inherited reference.
Does the distinction between I and II reflect transitivity of the promised item or merely a stem variant? These few examples do not settle the paradigm.
Keep Arabic yaqul outside productive Turoyo qwl indexing; a Turoyo ordinary-saying sense would require a vernacular clause, not an Arabic quotation.
